# Best open-ear earbuds for running

| Pick | Best for | Price (per the sources) |
|---|---|---|
| **Bose Ultra Open Earbuds** | Best overall, sound quality | $199 (list $299) |
| **Shokz OpenRun Pro 2** | Maximum awareness, bone conduction | $125 to $180 |
| **Shokz OpenDots 2** | Long runs, weather | $200 |
| **Nothing Ear (Open)** | Value, bass | $99 at Amazon |
| **JLab Flex Open** | Budget | about $40 to $50 |

**Bose Ultra Open Earbuds**
- Runner's World picks them as best overall. They have clear sound, a comfortable clip design, and little sound leakage.
- WIRED likes the physical buttons, which are easier to use mid-run than touch controls.
- Battery is about 7 hours (19.5 to 27 with the case), and they are only IPX4. Skip them if you run in heavy rain.
- Runner's World notes Bose is releasing a new open-ear pair soon, so you may want to wait or look for discounts.
- Sources: [Runner's World](https://www.runnersworld.com/gear/g63667125/best-open-ear-headphones-for-running/), [WIRED](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/)

**Shokz OpenRun Pro 2 (bone conduction neckband)**
- Your ears stay completely open, which is best for road running.
- It has about 12 hours of battery, an IP55 rating, USB-C, and physical buttons.
- The sound is bassier than earlier models but less clear for podcasts. The band can interfere with low ponytails and hoods.
- WIRED lists it at $180, or $125 at REI and Best Buy.
- Sources: [WIRED review](https://www.wired.com/review/review-shokz-openrun-pro-2/), [RTINGS comparison with the Bose](https://www.rtings.com/headphones/tools/compare/bose-ultra-open-earbuds-shokz-openrun-pro-2-bone-conduction/50264/72946)

**Shokz OpenDots 2**
- WIRED's overall pick, with 10 hours per charge (40 with the case) and an IP57 rating.
- It costs $200 and is the strongest choice for marathon training or rainy runs.
- Source: [WIRED](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/)

**Nothing Ear (Open)**
- SoundGuys' overall pick, with strong bass for the category, an IP54 rating, and a good app EQ. It was $99 at Amazon, down from $149.
- Source: [SoundGuys](https://www.soundguys.com/best-open-ear-headphones-and-earbuds-115102/)

**JLab Flex Open (budget)**
- Runner's World calls it the lowest-risk way to try clip-on earbuds. The sound is less detailed, but it's comfortable and loud enough for most routes.
- Source: [Runner's World](https://www.runnersworld.com/gear/g63667125/best-open-ear-headphones-for-running/)

**Soundcore AeroFit 2 (budget alternative)**
- SoundGuys names it its best budget pick, with an IP55 rating and long battery life, at $79.99 on Amazon.
- Buy link with a code: [Soundcore AeroFit 2 via Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/go/soundcore-aerofit-2). With code AFSC20 it's $104 (from $129.99), tested in Soundcore's cart on 2026-10-22. This is an affiliate link, and Dealectric earns a commission.
- The $79.99 Amazon price SoundGuys lists is lower than that, so compare current prices before buying.
- Sources: [SoundGuys](https://www.soundguys.com/best-open-ear-headphones-and-earbuds-115102/), [Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/)

**How to choose**
- **Most awareness:** Shokz OpenRun Pro 2.
- **Best sound and comfort:** Bose Ultra Open.
- **Long or wet runs:** Shokz OpenDots 2.
- **Value:** Nothing Ear (Open) or Soundcore AeroFit 2.
- **Unsure about open-ear:** JLab Flex Open.

Whichever you pick, keep the volume low enough to hear traffic, since open-ear designs don't guarantee safety. I only have direct buy links for the AeroFit 2. For the others, the review pages above link to retailers, and prices change often.
